_comment: The reading queue. Stage 4 appends here instead of filling a gap with a plausible sentence; scripts/synthesis_status.py renders the open ones. gap-001 to gap-003 were raised by the seed extraction passes on GA 19 and GA 20; gap-004 to gap-006 by the first Stage 4 pass.

gaps.question: GA 18 sits between GA 19 and the rest of the Marburg courses on any account of the development of care, but its commentary states no semester, so it cannot be placed on the ledger spine at all.
gaps.needs: The semester, from the commentary itself - i.e. from the volume the commentary works from, written into the commentary's opening note. Then chronology.json can move it from unresolved.
gaps.resolution: Summer Semester 1924, taken from GA 18 itself - the title page gives "Marburger Vorlesung Sommersemester 1924" [Marburg lecture course, summer semester 1924] and Michalski's afterword records a four-hour course at the Philipps University - and written into the commentary's opening note. chronology.json now carries stratum ga18-1924, and the sorge ledger orders GA 18 (1924) immediately before GA 19 (1924-25) and GA 20 (1925), which is the sequence the periodization turns on.

gaps.question: GA 20 § 31 dates the first striking on the phenomenon of care to seven years before the course, in work on the ontological foundations of Augustinian anthropology. Nothing in the corpus covers that work, so the earliest stratum of care is asserted in the corpus and evidenced nowhere in it.
gaps.needs: A commentary on the Augustine course the passage refers to. Until then the claim stands as a report of GA 20, not as a dated stratum.

gaps.question: GA 20 § 31 gives care a two-moment formal structure - being-ahead-of-itself in already-being-alongside. Whether the structure gains, loses or reorders a moment two years later cannot be checked from this ledger.
gaps.needs: An extraction pass for sorge over heidegger-sein-und-zeit-commentary (the densest file in the corpus for these terms, no record) and heidegger-being-and-time-commentary.

gaps.question: GA 19's commentary contains one occurrence of Sorge, in its own glossary, and three checked absences at the phronesis and eudaimonia sections - where the argument runs in the vocabulary of aletheuein and praxis. Whether that near-absence belongs to the course or to the commentary's rendering cannot be told from the ledger: the extraction checked German terms, and an English-language commentary may render a German term of art into ordinary English without flagging it.
gaps.needs: A second extraction pass over GA 19 keyed to the structure rather than the word - places where a being is said to be one for which its own being is at issue - so that a structural presence can be distinguished from a terminological absence. Partly answered from the side of GA 18: the SS 1924 pass records the same near-absence at that course's phronesis material (the hexis of aletheuein, GA 18 § 22), where the argument again runs in aletheuein and hexis, while the structural claim - Dasein as concern is care about itself - is made openly at § 17. So the absence is not an artifact peculiar to GA 19's commentary. The structural pass over GA 19 is still wanted.

gaps.question: sorge/ga20/005 is recorded as 'revised': concern is subordinated to care, having carried the earlier analysis of everyday commerce with the world. The ledger holds no unit for that earlier use, because the GA 20 pass covered Chapter Four only. A revision with no baseline in the ledger is an unsupported claim about a development.
gaps.needs: Extraction of GA 20 §§ 19-26, where the earlier use of Besorgen would be recorded. Until then the 'revised' status rests on the commentary's own retrospective phrasing rather than on two dated units.

gaps.question: The GA 20 § 35 absence - conscience and being-guilty treated without the vocabulary of care, next to a death analysis in § 34 that uses it - is either a fact about the course or an artifact of a commentary section that runs to 358 words. The extraction record flags the ambiguity and cannot resolve it.
gaps.needs: Either a fuller commentary on GA 20 §§ 33-36, or a note in the existing commentary recording whether the course itself drops the term there. This is the general case of a checked absence in a compressed section, and worth settling once as a rule.

gaps.question: marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-20-the-name-out-of-play records Marion reading Descartes' geometrical figures and God's essence alike as 'true and immutable natures', innate ideas drawn from thought rather than from sense-perception or imagination. Whether Husserl's eidos/Wesen is this doctrine's phenomenological heir, and whether he would count it as a 'phenomenological residuum' in his own technical sense (Ideas I) or only as the invariant residue of eidetic/free variation (Experience and Judgment), cannot be answered from the corpus: a keyword search of husserl-krisis-commentary, husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary, husserliana-9-phenomenological-psychology-commentary, husserliana-39-die-lebenswelt-commentary and husserl-thing-and-space-commentary for 'immutable' and 'residuum' turns up only an unrelated sense of residuum (the hyletic/transcendental residuum of the reduction, not essences), and no commentary discusses vera et immutabilis natura or cites Descartes' Meditation V by name.
gaps.needs: An extraction pass for theme 'wesen' over the Wesen/Wesensschau sections of husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary (the doctrine of essences, Ideas I §§ 2-3 and 22-23) and, if a commentary on Erfahrung und Urteil's free-variation chapters exists or is written, over its eidos/invariant material - to find or confirm the absence of any place where Husserl's own commentary explicitly compares eidetic essences to Descartes' true and immutable natures, and to settle whether 'phenomenological residuum' is ever used there of essences rather than only of transcendental consciousness.

gaps.question: husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary sits on the ledger spine at 1912 on a single stratum, but three of its intentionality units (intentionalitaet/hua5/020-022: the description of the intentional object as such, the intentional object as ideal index of consciousness-manifolds, the constitutive analysis of object-categories) carry the primary citation 'Ideas III, Afterword Section 6'. The ledger dates the Afterword only by the volume. Whether those three units precede or follow Ideas I's noema doctrine (1913-1928), Hua 7's sense-giving consciousness (1923-24) or FTL's correlation of object-category and evidence-category (1929) cannot be told, and the narrative has had to cite them without a place in the sequence.
gaps.needs: The Ideas III commentary to state, from the volume it works from, the date of the Afterword it comments on; then a second stratum in chronology.json for that text, and the three units re-tagged to it. Never a date supplied from memory.

gaps.question: The Sixth Logical Investigation enters the ledger at 1921 because its commentary reads the second-edition (B2) text and chronology.json carries only that stratum, whereas the Fifth Investigation spans 1901 to 1913 on two strata. The doctrine of intention and fulfilment, fullness as a third moment beside quality and matter, 'intention is not expectation', and categorial intuition in founded acts (intentionalitaet/lu6/001-024) therefore sit on the spine after the 1919 Natur und Geist lectures and beside the passive-synthesis lectures. At the same time none of the 41 Fifth Investigation units carries a stratum tag, although the commentary is recorded (chronology note) as marking first-edition-only passages and second-edition footnotes throughout; only hua19-1/022 states its edition in its own claim. Every ordering claim in the narrative that runs from the Investigations forward is exposed to this.
gaps.needs: Partly settled by the strata re-tagging pass of 2026-09-15, which changed no unit and no quote. For LU V: the commentary marks its editorial layers throughout, but inside this record's covered range (SS 9-21, 37-39, the Appendix) it assigns exactly one passage to an edition - the S 16 footnote - now tagged lu5-b-1913. The passages it does mark by edition (S 6's first-edition bundle doctrine and its second-edition recantation, S 7 struck in B and printed in smaller type, S 8's first-edition voice and its second-edition footnote and Addendum) all lie in Chapter One, which the intentionalitaet pass does not cover, so the remaining 40 units are untagged as a checked fact and the ledger now prints them under 'Stratum not assigned by the commentary'. Closing the LU V half needs an intentionalitaet pass over Chapter One (SS 1-8), where the marked A/B layers and the pure-ego recantations are. For LU VI nothing was taggable and the gap is unchanged in substance but sharper in diagnosis: re-checked against the whole commentary, it nowhere dates the A-text and nowhere marks a single A/B divergence in its body, although its opening says significant ones would be noted. So this half cannot be closed by tagging at all. It needs the commentary itself to record the first-edition layer and its date from the volume - Husserliana XIX/2 prints both texts - after which a first-edition stratum can go into chronology.json and units can be tagged. The 1901 date in that record's extractor.note is not usable: it is nowhere in the commentary, and CLAUDE.md rule 6 forbids supplying it from memory.

gaps.question: Three recorded statements of the objectivating thesis cannot be ordered. Hua XXVIII Part II s 9 (intentionalitaet/hua28/005): in the proper sense only objectivating acts are directed upon the objective, valuing acts upon values. Ideas II s 7 (hua4/010): every non-objectivating act is itself objectivating in what it newly contributes. Ideas I s 117 (hua3-i/005): all acts whatsoever, including sentiment and will, are objectivating. The ledger dates them 1908-09 to 1914, 1912 to 1928, and 1913 to 1928; the ranges overlap and no unit carries a stratum. Whether Ideas I s 117 revises Hua XXVIII s 9 or restates it under the widened sense of 'objectivating' that LU V s 37 (hua19-1/038) had already introduced is the hinge of the reception critiques (Bernet bernet-vds/029-030, Henry henry-em/012-013), and the ledger cannot turn it.
gaps.needs: Half settled by the strata re-tagging pass of 2026-09-15, which changed no unit and no quote. Hua XXVIII is now dated at the passage. The record turned out to span two courses, not one: the commentary covers Part A (the 1914 course) and Part B (the 1911 course Grundprobleme der Ethik und Wertlehre), and units 001-003 come from Einleitung S 8 of Part B. So hua28/005, the statement that in the proper sense only objectivating acts are directed upon the objective, is 1914 - a point date, not the 1908-09 to 1914 range the narrative had to use - while hua28/001-003, the transposition of the apophantic apparatus onto the will, is 1911, earlier than Ideas I. A hua28-1911 stratum was added to chronology.json on the commentary's own Part B opening, and the record's coverage note, which had wrongly listed the 1911 course as not covered, was corrected. Ideas II cannot be tagged, and that is now a checked fact rather than a gap in tagging, which is the outcome this gap asked for. The commentary dates the volume's layers and says in so many words why a section number will not stand in for one: parts of the 1912 draft were incorporated into the first 33 paragraphs 'in a criss-cross fashion', SS 18, 25 and 33 were expanded again in the 1918 working-out, the text from p. 143 onward was assembled anew without the commentary saying which S that is, and the third section rests on a manuscript written in 1913 that Stein expanded from other analyses. A hua4-1913 stratum was added for that manuscript, carrying no units, as hua28-1908-09 does. What remains open is the ordering itself, and it is now a two-term problem rather than a three-term one. Hua XXVIII S 9 is 1914; Ideas II S 7 is unassignable; Ideas I S 117 sits under a single 1913-1928 stratum because that commentary records the three editions as almost entirely identical. Deciding whether Ideas I S 117 revises Hua XXVIII S 9 or restates it under the widened sense of 'objectivating' of LU V S 37 now needs either the Ideas I commentary to record whether S 117 stands unchanged across the three editions - which would fix it at 1913, before 1914 - or an intentionalitaet pass over the Hua XXVIII sections that Part B's Schlussstuck and the 1908/09 layer would touch.

gaps.question: The status of the lowest layer reverses direction across three records and the ledger cannot say whether Husserl decided it. Hua XLIII/2 Part III s 4 (1911; intentionalitaet/hua43-2/009, 005) places the deepest-lying intentionality in the inner consciousness that constitutes the immanent time-flux, constituting through intentionality yet not through acts. Ideas I ss 82-83 (1913-28) carry two recorded absences: the time-structure of the stream is analysed without the theme, which the absence notes read as deferral. The Hua XXXIII record (1917-18; hua33/002, 004, 006, 007, 010) reports the editors as saying Husserl no longer took for granted that the primal process is an objectifying intentional consciousness, that it may be pre-intentional, and that the manuscripts reached no definitive determination. Every one of the fourteen Hua XXXIII units comes from the editors' introduction; the six main text groups (Texts 1-22) are unextracted. Bernet (bernet-vds/049, 053) then reads absolute consciousness as no longer intentional and not absolute.
gaps.needs: An extraction pass over the Hua XXXIII text groups themselves (Texts 1-22), keyed to primal process / Urprozess, pre-intentional, Laengsintentionalitaet / Querintentionalitaet, and to the apprehension-schema, recording where the texts decide, waver, or drop the question, and recording absences where a text treats the primal stream without the vocabulary. The same pass should settle whether the Ideas I ss 82-83 absence is the deferral the absence notes call it or a doctrinal separation.

gaps.question: The founding of intentionality in transcendence, the thesis on which the Heidegger side of the narrative turns, reaches the ledger only through a reception record. Bernet (bernet-vds/004, 008, 009) reports Heidegger's formula that intentionality is the ratio cognoscendi of transcendence and transcendence the ratio essendi of intentionality, intentionality as ontic transcendence grounded in the Urtranszendenz of being-in-the-world; the Bernet pass note assigns those chapters to the 1925 course. On the primary side the GA 20 record covers ss 5-6 and 11-13 and holds no such unit; the GA 24 record has three units and its pass note names the intentio/intentum analysis, the misinterpretations and the transcendence relation as not covered; Sein und Zeit contributes only the s 69(b) note (sz/021, 023). So the narrative can say that Heidegger keeps the word and moves the question, and cannot cite from the primary side where he grounds it.
gaps.needs: Extraction for intentionalitaet over the GA 24 commentary's uncovered material on perception (intentio/intentum, misinterpretations, intentionality and transcendence), and over GA 20 ss 4 and 7-10, which the GA 20 pass note lists as not covered. Then the Bernet units can be checked against dated primary units instead of standing in for them.

gaps.question: In the Sein und Zeit record (23 units) the recorded quotes carry the word 'intentionality' or 'intentional' in three units only: sz/022 and sz/023, both reporting the s 69(b) note, and sz/008, where the phrase 'intentionality is here out-radicalized' is the commentator's own. The pass note says the record covers the points where the treatise engages and displaces intentionality, but no absence is recorded for any Sein und Zeit section. The narrative therefore cannot say whether the word is absent from ss 12-13 and ss 43-44 in the treatise as the commentary renders it, or only absent from the quotes the extraction chose. The second commentary on the treatise (heidegger-being-and-time-commentary) has one term hit and no record.
gaps.needs: Absence records with absent_terms keyed to Intentionalitaet / intentional (not to 'directedness' or 'of', which are ordinary English) for Sein und Zeit ss 12-13, 43(a), 44(b) and 69(b) in heidegger-sein-und-zeit-commentary, and an intentionalitaet pass over heidegger-being-and-time-commentary, so that the near-disappearance of the word becomes a checked negative rather than an impression from the extracted quotes.

gaps.question: The Krisis commentary (intentionalitaet/krisis/009, Crisis s 46) records Husserl dating the first breakthrough of the universal correlation-a priori to about 1898, during the working-out of the Logical Investigations. The ledger's earliest dated unit is 1901, and its earliest recorded statement of the correlation as a principle is Ideas III s 7 (1912; hua5/003) and Ideas I s 86 (hua3-p34/007). LU V s 20 (hua19-1/029) says the opposite in emphasis: for the really phenomenological consideration the objectivity itself is nothing. The earliest stratum of the correlation is thus asserted in the corpus, as Husserl's retrospection, and evidenced nowhere in it. This is the same shape as gap-002 on care.
gaps.needs: No commentary in the corpus reaches 1898. The nearest unread candidates are husserl-prolegomena-commentary (2 term hits, no record) and husserliana-26-theory-of-meaning-commentary (7 hits, no record); an extraction pass over each, keyed to correlation / Korrelation and to the a priori of the object-consciousness relation, would show whether the doctrine is stated before Ideas III. Until then the 1898 date stands as a report of the Krisis, not as a dated stratum.

gaps.question: intentionalitaet/eu/003 (Erfahrung und Urteil s 8: the original induction or anticipation proves to be a modification-mode of originally instituting cognitive activities, a mode of intentionality that intends beyond a core of givenness) and intentionalitaet/hua39/023 (Hua XXXIX Text Nr. 15, dated 1934 in chronology.json: the original induction or anticipation proves to be a modification-mode of originally instituting activity, a mode of intentionality, the anticipating meaning beyond a kernel of givenness) record the same sentence in nearly the same words. Erfahrung und Urteil is chronology-unresolved, for want of the volume in the sources repository (STATUS.md), so the ledger holds it out of the sequence. The parallel is dating evidence the pipeline cannot yet register, and it must not be used to place the undated record.
gaps.needs: Per STATUS.md, the volume in faultynode/sources first, then the Landgrebe compilation strata written into the commentary's opening note and into chronology.json. Once a stratum exists, record the relation between eu/003 and hua39/023 as a unit with the appropriate status (presupposed or revised) rather than as a coincidence noted in prose.

gaps.question: Hua XLIII/2 Part III s 4 (1911; intentionalitaet/hua43-2/013, status criticized) records an objection Husserl raises against his own layering of primary content, feeling-apprehension and value-intentionality: extended to the drive-sphere it fails, because the drive toward the continuation of an agreeable tone already has a directedness-toward whose striving intention fulfils itself, so drive admits no layer of non-intentional primary content. The ledger records the objection as raised and not as answered. Henry (1963; henry-em/012-013) and Bernet (1994; bernet-vds/029-030) later treat the intentionality of affectivity as Husserl's settled thesis and criticize it as such. Whether Husserl answered the 1911 objection, and where, is not in the corpus as extracted: the Hua XLIII/2 pass covered Part III ss 1 and 4 only, and the passive-synthesis record has four units.
gaps.needs: Extraction for intentionalitaet over Hua XLIII/2 Parts I-II and Part III ss 2-3, and over the affection and association material of husserliana-11-analyses-concerning-passive-and-active-synthesis-commentary, keyed to Trieb / drive, Streben / striving, Tendenz, and affection, recording whether a non-intentional drive-layer is asserted, denied, or left open.

gaps.question: LU V s 11 (intentionalitaet/hua19-1/009) says the so-called immanent object is in truth not immanent or mental at all. Ideas I s 90 (hua3-p34/012) rejects the immanent object as inner image by a regress. Hua VII, Fifteenth Lecture (1923-24; hua7-i/003, 006) then calls the object of the intentional relation the mere intentional object, the immanent one, as Brentano too introduces it, and denies only that this immanence is real (reell). Kern (kern-hk/018) reports a distinction of real from intentional immanence. The ledger has the two ends and a reception gloss; it has no dated unit between 1913 and 1923 in which Husserl reappropriates the word for the intentional object or marks that he is doing so, and the narrative cannot say whether this is a terminological reversal or a continuity under a changed sense of 'immanent'.
gaps.needs: Extraction for intentionalitaet over husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary (1910; 14 term hits, no record) and over the First Chapter of the Hua VII commentary, keyed to immanent / Immanenz, reell, and irreal, recording where the word is applied to the intentional object and with what qualification.
